note: Outputs are advice, not artefacts, so the assertions check for the presence of specific reasoning the skill exists to install — not for a file format.

evals.name: matches-numbers-looks-wrong
evals.prompt: Модель торса сходится с артом и по фасу, и по профилю — везде в пределах 5 мм при допуске 8. А выглядит всё равно не так, и я не могу понять почему. Что смотреть?
evals.expected_output: Should say that measurement is blind to form (a bounding box is the same for an oval and a rounded rectangle), and send the user to the view from above and an orbit — the two views orthographic projections cannot replace. Should not propose taking more measurements.
assertions: Names the view from above as the thing to look at, and says why: a section's shape is invisible from every other angle
Names an orbit or rotation as necessary, and says why: ridges standing edge-on to the orthographic cameras are invisible in them
States explicitly that agreeing measurements cannot rule out a form defect, rather than suggesting more or finer measurements
Does not propose fixing anything before looking

evals.name: blockout-setup-from-turnaround
evals.prompt: Starting a character torso from a three-view turnaround for a game — roughly 3k triangles for this part. I've got the reference images and Blender open. How should I set this up before I touch geometry?
evals.expected_output: Should derive the budget from purpose and reference rather than accepting 3k uncritically, set up the scene and reference planes, produce markup as a control instrument rather than a blueprint to build from, and say plainly that the build itself is located by eye on the reference — not by a table of sections.
assertions: Treats the polygon budget as something derived from purpose and the reference, not as a given number to fill
Covers scene setup and reference placement before any geometry
States that markup is used for checking, and that operations are located by eye on the reference rather than by a table of numbers
Does not hand back a table of cross-sections to model to

evals.name: armhole-without-pole-ring
evals.prompt: I need to attach an arm to a torso mesh in Blender. The concept art has a sleeve seam I was going to cut along, but last time I did that I ended up with a pole at almost every step around the opening. How do I cut it this time?
evals.expected_output: Should say the opening is cut along the mesh's own lines — a rectangle in (ring, column) coordinates — not along the drawn seam, because a diagonal cut across the grid makes a staircase and every step becomes a pole. Should note that the seam is decoration and belongs in texture or a shallow groove, not in topology.
assertions: Says to cut along the mesh's own ring and column lines rather than along the drawn seam
Explains that a diagonal cut across the grid produces a staircase and a pole per step
States the expected result: a grid-aligned opening yields exactly four poles, at the corners
Says the drawn seam belongs in texture or a shallow groove rather than in topology
